chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding the man who transfers the debt of another man to a third party.

So the one who transferred it says to him, 'You are free from what I owe you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he frees him (from the debt), then it is not for him to return to him (the debtor), and if he does not free him, then it is for him to return to the one who transferred it (the creditor).

key_terms.يُحِيلُ: Transfers (a debt/claim from one person to another)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on transferring a debt and can the creditor reclaim it from the original debtor?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanics of *hiyal* (debt assignment) by distinguishing between a mere transfer of claim and a full discharge (*ibra*). It establishes that the creditor's right to recourse against the original debtor hinges on whether the transfer included an explicit waiver of the debt, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the intention behind financial transactions. This ruling ensures clarity in commercial contracts, preventing ambiguity when debts are assigned to third parties.
